resources.string: Light’s own tools — Messages, Notes, Directory — draw their keyboard themselves and keep it whatever you choose here. Bright Keyboard appears in the apps you install yourself.
Names and anything else the dictionary doesn\'t know. Added words are never autocorrected away, can be corrected to, and can be swiped.
Words you held down in the suggestion strip. They\'re still spelled correctly — the keyboard just stops offering them.
Nothing for that. Try a shorter word.
GIF search needs a key. Add one in Settings.
That didn\'t go through. Try again, or pick another.
GIF copied \u2014 paste it if it didn\'t appear
Nothing starred yet. Hold a GIF to keep it.
The GIF button on the tools page searches KLIPY. It is the one thing in this keyboard that uses the network \u2014 everything else, the dictionary and the swipe model included, runs on the phone.
Optional. The key built into the app is shared by everyone running it, so when it is spent the search says so. A key of your own from %1$s has its own allowance.
Nothing copied yet. What you copy in other apps shows up here.
Clipboard history is off. Turn it on in Settings.
A small neural network, bundled and run on the phone. Right first time about 93%% of the time, against 75%% for the older method, measured on the same real swipes.
Compares your trace against the path through each word\'s keys. What this keyboard used before, and still what answers if the model can\'t load.
The model stopped the keyboard twice on this phone, so it is not being loaded. Swipes are read by shape matching. Tap Model above to try it again.
Crowd the keys against one edge so a thumb can reach all of them. The empty strip carries a button that puts the keyboard back to full width.
One tap per letter. The dictionary works out the word, and delete shows the other words those taps could be.
Press 2 three times for C. No prediction at all — it types exactly the letter you pressed.
Only clear typos and missing apostrophes. Everything else is offered, not applied.
Also fixes words spelled the way they sound, and missing spaces. Recommended.
Fixes more, guesses wrong more often. Fastest to type against.
After a fix, press delete to see the next-best word. Keep pressing to get back to exactly what you typed.
After a fix, one press puts back what you typed. Swiped words still show alternatives.
Only words close to what you drew. A trace that matches nothing gives nothing.
Always finds a word, even for a rough trace. More wrong guesses.
Each press shows the next-best reading of the trace. The last one deletes.
One press takes the whole traced word back out, the way one gesture put it in. The other readings stay in the suggestion strip.
The word you drew is almost always in the first four. More of them means fewer retypes when it is not the first.
Used for every emoji that has one. Hold an emoji in the panel to pick a different tone or a gendered version just for that one.
Type the name of a thing and its emoji appears in the suggestion strip. Needs Suggestions turned on.
Where your taps for each key really land. The keyboard reads an unclear tap against this and never moves a key on screen.
Clipboard, emoji, GIFs, one hand, and hide the keyboard.
Straight to the emoji panel, skipping the toolbox.
Leave the key off. The row closes up around it.
Takes the labels off, leaving a bump under F and J the way a real keyboard does. Space, return, delete and the rest stay. Worth trying once the keys have learned your hand.
Type here to watch it move

On each key: a line and dot to where your taps for it land, a shaded box for the part no spelling model may overrule, an oval for how loosely you hit it against your own average, and the taps counted. Faint means barely measured.
%1$d taps counted. Targets have shifted %2$d%% of a key from where they started.
Nothing measured yet. Type in the field below and watch the keys fill in.
Tap the field below to open the keyboard.
The phone pad types digits, so there is no per-letter touch model to draw. Switch to a letter layout to see one.
A plain text file, one word to a line. Anything after the word on a line is ignored, so a frequency list or a spreadsheet column works as it is. Importing replaces whatever was imported before.
Imported %1$d words. %2$d lines held nothing this keyboard can type.
Nothing in that file could be used. It needs one word to a line.
That file could not be read.
No file picker on this phone.

Which dictionaries autocorrect and swipe typing work against. Tap to switch one on or off. More than one at a time is allowed, and worth knowing about: each list says how common a word is within its own language, so two at once says either could be the one you are typing.
From the AOSP dictionaries at codeberg.org/Helium314/aosp-dictionaries. Nothing is stored here; the phone fetches the list you pick straight from that project.
Could not reach the dictionary list. Check the connection.
%1$d languages available. Search to narrow it down.

The keys do not change. A missing accent key costs nothing, because typing cafe finds café and ol finds øl. Pick the key arrangement itself under Keyboard layout. A language whose letters are not a to z cannot be used here, and says so when you try.
Drag to move it. Pinch to resize it.
Moving to a new app \u2014 tap to switch
All moved \u2014 tap to remove this one
BrightKeyboard is moving to a new app

This keyboard is a fork of Adam Weber\'s light-keyboard. When I forked it I kept his app ID, and that turned out to block him from listing his own keyboard. So I\'m giving the ID back and taking one of my own.
Android treats a new ID as a new app, so this is an install, not an update.
2 \u00b7 Open it once. Your settings, saved words and the typing model it learned come across automatically.
Nothing else changes. Same keyboard, same key, same repo.
Couldn\'t open BrightMarket. Search for BrightKeyboard there, or find it at brightmarket.gzl.dev.
The new BrightKeyboard is installed. Pick it in your keyboard settings if you haven\'t yet, then remove this one \u2014 it stops getting updates from here.
